messages:
morgan: Quick async standup — GPU headroom snapshot

morgan: YESTERDAY: drained two H100 nodes in us-west for kernel upgrade, ran soak on warmup lanes
morgan: BLOCKERS: saw a 6% eviction spike on prewarm jobs after drain, not sure if it's quota or spot churn
morgan: TODAY: re-run prewarm in small batches, submit quota ticket if needed, ping for PR review

ashley: FYI — I pushed a quick fix to the autoscaler thresholds (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1428)
ashley: after that, us-central headroom improved ~12% during synthetic load
ashley: still seeing intermittent throttles in eu-west1 for A100 pools

ryan: filed cloud quota request CLOUD-4823 for additional A100s in eu-west1, ETA 48-72h
ryan: request assigned to @cloud-ops, cc @sophia

sophia: I'll take the triage on evictions, starting with logs from prewarm controllers
sophia: can someone run `kubectl logs -n prewarm prewarm-controller-0 --since=2h` and drop output in the ticket? :mag:

infra-oncall-bot: [alert] spot-evictions eu-west1: 3 events in 1h — linked to nodegroup-tilt-canary

ashley: pasted logs snippet into CLOUD-4823; initial look shows kubelet OOMs on a couple of nodes
ashley: could be memory pressure from experimental batching config — rolling that back now

morgan: thanks. also pinging for a quick code review for the canary scaling tweak, @ryan if you have 10m
morgan: if we need an immediate buffer, can we temporarily route low-priority requests to dedicated fallback pool? any objections?

ryan: agree, fallback routing looks safe for now. I'll open a quick rollback plan and set a small canary (5% traffic) :ok_hand:

sophia: once I finish triage I'll post a short RCA and propose mitigations (autoscaler thresholds + pod mem limits)

morgan: TL;DR — health noisy but manageable. Action items: ashley rollback batching patch, ryan follow quota ticket, sophia triage evictions, morgan coordinate canary. Ping here when done :thumbsup:
